title: chat.gsi.de — Overview
description: Traffic, authentication, chat usage and process health. Everything here comes from the frontend's single /metrics endpoint.

panels.title: Data flow and saturation
panels.description: A weathermap: edges carry throughput, nodes carry health. A node's number is its p95 latency as a PERCENTAGE OF ITS OWN BUDGET, which is what makes Postgres and the LLM proxy comparable on one screen despite latencies four orders of magnitude apart — the bottleneck is the highest number. Over 100% means that hop is slower than we consider acceptable; the budgets are listed in deploy/grafana/nodegraph.py. Nodes reading 0 with 'not measured' have no latency instrumentation, not zero latency. Built entirely from Prometheus with label_replace, so there is no topology source to keep in sync.

panels.title: Where the time goes
panels.description: The same saturation numbers as the graph, ranked. Read the top bar as 'this is the component to look at first'. Anything under 50% is comfortable; over 100% means that hop is exceeding the budget set for it, which is a judgement call written down in deploy/grafana/nodegraph.py rather than a law of nature.

panels.title: Frontend
panels.description: The single scrape target. 0 here means every other panel is stale, not zero.

panels.title: Backends reachable
panels.description: Postgres, SeaweedFS, Valkey, Keycloak and the runtime, as seen from the last scrape.

panels.title: Version
panels.description: APP_VERSION baked into the running image.

panels.title: Requests per second by status
panels.description: Status is the exact code. Thrown redirects and error() calls are counted too, so 303s from the login gate show up here.

panels.title: Latency (time to response)
panels.description: Time until the Response object exists, NOT until the last byte. /api/chat returns its SSE stream immediately and then runs for minutes; turn latency lives on the LLM dashboard.

panels.title: Denied by the auth gate
panels.description: not_admin spiking usually means someone shared an /admin link, not an attack.

panels.title: Auth events
panels.description: token_exchange_failed with healthy login_start is the client-secret mismatch described in AGENTS.md §6.

panels.title: Chat turns per hour by mode
Turn duration p95 by mode
panels.description: gsi-deep is budgeted 180s of wall clock (DEEP_WALL_CLOCK_BUDGET_S); a p95 pressed against that ceiling means answers are being truncated.

panels.title: Budget exhausted (1h)
panels.description: Deep turns cut short by the wall-clock budget and answered from partial findings.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: The frontend Deployment is capped at 1 GiB; rss approaching it means an OOMKill and a rollout, not a slowdown.

panels.title: Event-loop lag
panels.description: Sampled on a 5s timer, not during the scrape -- measuring it inside /metrics would report the scrape's own fan-out.

panels.title: Backend reachability
panels.description: A collector at 0 with the frontend at 1 means that ONE backend is unreachable and its panels are stale. Both at 0 means the whole exposition is gone -- these must not be confused.

panels.title: Keycloak readiness
panels.description: Probed on the management port (9000). Keycloak here is start-dev with an ephemeral H2 database, so 'is login working' is the only fact about it worth graphing.

panels.title: Postgres queries per second
panels.description: Counted when a query is awaited, which is also what keeps SQL fragments (retrieval.ts builds them with the same tag) out of the numbers.

panels.title: Valkey cache hit ratio
panels.description: Sessions are the only thing in Valkey, so a falling ratio means sessions are expiring faster than they are used -- people being logged out, not a cache problem.

panels.title: Open handles and descriptors
panels.description: A handle count that climbs and never falls is a leaked socket or timer; it precedes the memory graph noticing.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: A sawtooth on the frontend line is a crash loop; check the liveness probe before anything else.
